pass_rule: within: A, B fail over (at most one slot missed), C decides every slot as without the loss; beyond: C commits nothing and switches no feeder by command during the outage and resumes within two periods, A decides nothing and resumes within failover_s plus one period, B's four substations run their tables; no collapses
known_issues: C stands for D: the same code; they differ in who runs the validators (experiment 6)
a substation that holds keeps its feeders as they are and sheds only by UFLS; the island's load and supply keep changing, so a long hold can trip UFLS that a live decision would avoid
both centres of A come back as standby; the one that hears no heartbeat for failover_s takes over, so A's resumption includes the failover time

a validator back from an outage missed the substations' reports while it was away; until each substation's next report (at most one dispatch period) its own proposals leave reports out and the others refuse them (report-inclusion rule), so C resumes when a validator that stayed up proposes (up to about 400 s after a two-hour stop, column resume_max_s). Validators do not pass reports to each other, as a CometBFT mempool would on reconnect
